title: Rav Chana son of Rav Ketina
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Yuchasin cites that he was R-H’s student, and Seder HaDorot wrote “I have not found it.” Hyman says: “In truth, it is so in Pesachim 106a according to Dikdukei Soferim: Rav Chana son of Rav Ketina asked Rav Huna: One who tasted — may he make havdalah?” Hyman’s received reading is Rav Chana bar Chinena. In Yevamot 79a he raises an objection to R-H’s words. In Yoma 54b: “Rav Ketina said — Rav Chisda objected — Rav Nachman said — Rav Chisda objected — Rav Nachman said — Rav Chana son of Rav Ketina objected — he said to him: Do you say ‘she was divorced’?” etc. — and this refers to Rav Nachman, or he objects to Rav Ketina his father.

He is mentioned in Taanit 13a, Kiddushin 77b and Bekhorot 37b. Likewise in Nedarim 65b “R-H son of Rav Ketina raised a difficulty against Rabbah,” and the reading of the Rosh’s Piskei is Rav Chana. Likewise in Chullin 17b, “R-H son of Rav Ketina said that R-Sh-B-L said,” Dikdukei Soferim reads Rav Chana. In Zevachim 115a [1], Hyman quotes “R-H bar R-Q sat before Rav Chisda.” He reports “Rav Chana bar R-Q” as the reading of Shitah Mekubbetzet and the Bach. In Chullin 19a: “Rav Chanan son of Rav Ketina said to R-N: According to whom? — He said to him: I know neither chilak nor bilak,” etc.; Dikdukei Soferim reads Rav Chana.

The recovered Wikisource footnote corrects the citation to Zevachim 115b. The consulted text there gives Rav Huna bar Rav Ketina. Hyman prints 115a and attributes the reading Rav Chana to Shitah Mekubbetzet and the Bach. His printed notice reads והב״ח, whereas the supplied transcription reads ורב״ח.

The quoted exchange is on Yoma 54a in the consulted edition. The printed Hyman notice cites 54b and gives one objection by Rav Chisda and one reply by Rav Nachman, as in the consulted passage. The supplied transcription repeats both. Hyman leaves open whether Rav Chana objects to Rav Nachman or to his father Rav Ketina.

The consulted Rosh on Nedarim names Rav Chana bar Rav Ketina and Rabbah. The consulted Bavli at Nedarim 65b instead names Rav Huna bar Rav Ketina speaking to the rabbis. Chullin 19a has Rav Chanan addressing Rav Nachman, alongside the variant Chana reported by Hyman.
